meta.title: Trade-area and market evidence register
meta.rule: A value is only shown when it was read from the linked official page during this session. Where the official source could not supply a parcel- or trade-area-level figure, the value is left null and the row is flagged. Nothing is interpolated, averaged or estimated into a value field.
meta.geography_note: The subject property's address, parcel number and coordinates are private workspace material and are deliberately absent from this file. Geography labels below name the published statistical areas that were actually queried, not the parcel.

metrics.label: Population, July 1, 2025 (V2025 estimate)
metrics.source_name: U.S. Census Bureau, QuickFacts (V2025 population estimates)
metrics.note: City-level. Serves as an upper-bound proxy only; it is not a trade-area figure.

metrics.label: Population change, April 1 2020 base to July 1 2025
metrics.note: Published as a percent change by Census; reproduced as published.

metrics.label: Persons under 18 years
metrics.note: Relevant to school-driven household demand, not to quick-service trade area by itself.

metrics.label: Population per square mile
metrics.note: Land area 469.49 sq mi (2020, same source).

metrics.label: Persons living in same house 1 year ago (age 1+)
metrics.note: Residential stability indicator.

metrics.label: Median household income (2024 dollars)
metrics.note: City-level proxy. Trade-area median household income inside a 3-minute drive time was not obtainable from an official published page without disclosing the parcel location.

metrics.label: Persons in poverty
metrics.period: V2025-flagged series (QuickFacts: Persons in poverty, percent)
metrics.note: QuickFacts labels this series by estimate vintage; the page shows 16.5% at the time of reading.

metrics.label: Median household income, County (contrast)
metrics.note: County QuickFacts page failed to return content on repeated attempts (HTTP fetch error). Value deliberately left blank rather than taken from a secondary site.

metrics.label: Median value of owner-occupied housing units
metrics.note: Residential, not commercial. Useful only as a direction-of-wealth indicator for the trade area.

metrics.label: Median gross rent
metrics.note: Residential rent. Not a substitute for a commercial ground-lease comp.

metrics.label: Households
metrics.note: Persons per household 2.61 (same source).

metrics.label: Median selected monthly owner costs, with a mortgage
HUD Fair Market Rent, 2-bedroom, FY2026
metrics.geo: Los Angeles-Long Beach-Glendale HUD Metro FMR Area (31080)
metrics.source_name: HUD User, FY2026 Fair Market Rent Documentation System
metrics.note: The HUD calculation page rendered its methodology but the FMR value cells came back empty to this reader. Left blank; the page is linked so the figure can be read directly in a browser.

metrics.label: Smarter Balanced ELA / math proficiency, serving district of the parcel
metrics.source_name: California Department of Education, CAASPP Reporting
metrics.note: School-quality evidence requires the district/school code, which is derivable only from the private address. Deliberately not guessed. Use the linked official search once the address is available in the private workspace.

metrics.label: Unemployment rate, September 2026
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, LA Area Economic Summary (updated 2026-11-04), Local Area Unemployment Statistics
metrics.note: Comparative: Los Angeles County 4.5%, California 5.1%, United States 4.0% (same source, same month).

metrics.label: Unemployment rate, September 2025
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, LA Area Economic Summary
metrics.note: Year-over-year improvement of 1.1 percentage points in the metro rate.

metrics.label: Unemployment rate, latest month available (series query)
metrics.geo: Los Angeles-Long Beach-Glendale, CA Metropolitan Division
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Public Data API, series LAUMT063108000000003
metrics.note: Machine-read series confirms 4.4% for Sep-2026; Aug-2026 4.8%, Jul-2026 5.0%. Oct-2025 shows '-' (data unavailable due to the 2025 lapse in appropriations).

metrics.label: Total nonfarm employment, September 2026
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics via LA Area Economic Summary
metrics.note: +30.2 thousand (+0.5%) over the year.

metrics.label: Total nonfarm employment, latest month (series query)
metrics.geo: Los Angeles-Long Beach-Glendale, CA Metropolitan Division
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Public Data API, series SMU06310800000000001
metrics.note: Preliminary and subject to revision. Sep-2026 6,282.7; Sep-2025 6,251.9.

metrics.label: 12-month change in employment, Information sector
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics
metrics.note: Information lost 11.4 thousand jobs over the year; the steepest sectoral decline in the metro.

metrics.label: 12-month change in employment, Education and health services
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics
metrics.note: +49.1 thousand jobs, the largest sectoral gain; a stabiliser for lunch/near-hospital trade.

metrics.label: 12-month change in employment, Leisure and hospitality
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics
metrics.note: +11.5 thousand jobs.

metrics.label: Authorised employees, all industries, Q1 2026 (average weekly wage)
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, QCEW via LA Area Economic Summary
metrics.note: Orange County comparator on the same page: $1,766.

metrics.label: Mean travel time to work (workers 16+)
metrics.note: Commute length supports drive-thru demand in the aggregate, but not at any specific corner.

metrics.label: Total retail sales
metrics.note: Retail sales per capita $21,281 (same source, same year).

metrics.label: Total accommodation and food services sales
metrics.note: The closest official measure to food-away-from-home demand available at city level.

metrics.label: Total health care and social assistance receipts
CPI-U, all items, 12-month change
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index news release (2026-11-10)
metrics.note: United States all items the same month: 3.7% (BLS LA Area Economic Summary).

metrics.label: CPI-U, all items, 1-month change
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index news release (2026-11-10)
metrics.note: The 12-month change for October 2026 is not published: BLS did not collect October 2025 data because of the 2025 lapse in appropriations, so it cannot compute an October 2026 over-the-year change. This is an official data gap, not an error in this register.

metrics.label: Shelter, 1-month change
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index news release

metrics.label: Employment Cost Index, 12-month change in wages and salaries
metrics.geo: Los Angeles-Long Beach, CA Combined Statistical Area
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Cost Index via LA Area Economic Summary
metrics.note: United States 3.1% (same source). Relevant to the tenant's largest controllable cost.

metrics.label: Average hourly wage, all occupations
metrics.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, OEWS via LA Area Economic Summary

metrics.label: House price appreciation, 4 quarters (single-family, purchase-only)
metrics.source_name: Federal Housing Finance Agency, HPI Quarterly Report 2026Q3 (released 2026-11-24)
metrics.note: Pacific census division +0.5%; United States +2.5% over the same four quarters.

metrics.label: House price appreciation, 4 quarters, United States
metrics.source_name: Federal Housing Finance Agency, HPI Quarterly Report 2026Q3
metrics.note: Prior four-quarter readings on the same table: 2024Q3 4.4%, 2023Q3 5.1%, 2022Q3 11.4%.

metrics.label: House price appreciation, 4 quarters, Los Angeles MSA
metrics.source_name: Federal Housing Finance Agency, HPI Quarterly Report 2026Q3, tables of 100 largest MSAs
metrics.note: The MSA table sits on a later page of the report than the portion retrieved. Left blank rather than inferred from the state figure. A single-family index in any case is not a restaurant-cap-rate series.

metrics.label: Annual Average Daily Traffic at the nearest state-highway count station
metrics.note: Caltrans publishes AADT only for the State Highway System, in spreadsheet form keyed by route and post-mile. Selecting the correct station requires the private location. No value is asserted here.

metrics.label: City-street traffic count at the parcel frontage
metrics.source_name: Caltrans, Traffic Census Program (scope note) and City of Los Angeles Public Works / LADOT
metrics.note: Caltrans states that counts for city and county streets are held by the city traffic engineering or public works department. No official city count for this frontage has been read, so the row is blank.

metrics.label: Zoning, General Plan land-use designation and specific-plan overlay for the parcel
metrics.source_name: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning, ZIMAS / Case Search
metrics.note: ZIMAS is address-keyed. The lookup is specified as an offline workspace step (see Trade Area page, step 3) and is not published here because the result would identify the parcel.
